turns.question: What refund authority model do you want delegated to support: a hard per-refund ceiling with mandatory rationale and an escalation path above that threshold, or unrestricted authority? Recommended: cap support-initiated refunds at $100 per refund, require a reason code plus free-text rationale, and escalate anything above the ceiling to an owner approval path.

Should the delegated capability include partial refunds as well as full refunds, and if so should the same $100 ceiling apply to the refund amount actually issued rather than original charge value? Recommended: allow both full and partial refunds, enforcing the same $100 ceiling on the refunded amount.

contract.G: Delegate bounded refund execution to support without granting unrestricted payment authority.
contract.T: Add support-initiated refund capability with per-refund policy enforcement, reason capture, escalation for higher amounts, and immutable audit logging.
contract.S: Support role may issue full or partial refunds up to $100 per refund with a required reason; refunds above $100 require owner approval; record actor, amount, rationale, target payment, outcome, and approver when applicable.
contract.V: Verify RBAC denies unsupported actors, refunds above $100 cannot execute without owner approval, full and partial refunds within limit succeed, required reason is enforced, and audit events are emitted for every attempt and outcome.
contract.X: Stop if provider APIs cannot support policy-enforced partial/full refunds, owner approval cannot be represented transactionally, or audit logging cannot be made tamper-evident enough for billing operations.
contract.P: Persist the decision as a refund-authority policy and implement only after threshold, escalation, and audit semantics are fixed across product, API, and support tooling.

promotions.name: Refund authority
promotions.evidence: A stable policy term emerged: support can execute refunds only within a delegated limit, with larger refunds requiring owner involvement.

promotions.name: Delegated support refund policy
promotions.evidence: This is a consequential control decision because the repository lacks both an approval threshold and an audit event today, and the chosen model introduces both.

turns.question: What should the retention anchor and retained artifact set be for customer uploads that may still be referenced by completed reports? Recommended: delete uploads 90 days after the last report that references them reaches a terminal completed state, while retaining report summaries.

What user-facing deletion semantics do you want given disaster-recovery backups retain deleted objects for 30 days? Recommended: treat product-surface deletion as final immediately, disclose backup lag only in internal recovery policy, and do not offer user-initiated restore during the backup window.

contract.G: Automate cleanup of stale customer uploads without breaking completed-report records or misrepresenting deletion behavior.
contract.T: Define and enforce an upload-retention policy keyed to report lifecycle, delete eligible uploads automatically, preserve report summaries, and align user messaging with backup reality.
contract.S: Delete uploads 90 days after their last associated report finishes; retain report summaries; backups may still hold deleted objects for up to 30 days for disaster recovery only; user-facing semantics state deletion is final.
contract.V: Verify retention eligibility is computed from the last referencing report completion timestamp, summaries remain accessible after upload deletion, deleted uploads are not restorable through product workflows, and backup-held objects age out within the documented DR window.
contract.X: Stop if upload-to-report references cannot be resolved reliably, report completion state is not queryable as a retention anchor, or legal/compliance review rejects the 90-day policy.
contract.P: Persist this as the accepted retention policy before implementation so lifecycle jobs, support messaging, and recovery procedures all use the same semantics.

promotions.name: Retention anchor
promotions.evidence: A consequential term appeared: deletion timing depends on the timestamp when the last referencing report finishes.

promotions.name: Customer upload retention and deletion semantics
promotions.evidence: No accepted retention policy exists today, and the decision must reconcile active report references with 30-day disaster-recovery backups.

turns.question: Define the exact privacy boundary for 'local-only': which artifacts are prohibited from leaving the device, including provider calls and observability payloads? Recommended: file bytes, file metadata, and all derived text remain on-device, with no remote AI processing and no telemetry that can contain content-bearing excerpts.

contract.G: Provide file processing that is genuinely local-only rather than merely avoiding raw file upload.
contract.T: Replace any remote-content path with on-device processing and harden telemetry so no file content or derivatives can egress the device.
contract.S: Keep file bytes, metadata, and derived text entirely on-device, including AI processing and telemetry; use the existing on-device parser for the primary format; exclude any remote provider path for content-bearing operations.
contract.V: Verify no network path receives file bytes, metadata, or derived text; telemetry redacts or omits content-bearing payloads; the primary format is fully handled by the on-device parser; and failure paths do not leak excerpts.
contract.X: Stop if any required capability still depends on the remote AI provider, if telemetry cannot be configured to eliminate content-bearing excerpts, or if unsupported formats would silently fall back to remote processing.
contract.P: Persist local-only as an explicit data-boundary contract so product claims, architecture, and observability controls remain aligned as features evolve.

promotions.name: Local-only boundary
promotions.evidence: A stable boundary was defined: file bytes, metadata, and derived text must all remain on the device, including AI and telemetry.

promotions.name: Strict on-device processing for customer files
promotions.evidence: This is a consequential architecture decision because the current system sends derived text to a remote AI provider and telemetry may include excerpted payloads.
